text:
Multi-negative objectives are a strong SASRec ablation, but loss calibration matters alongside negative count. [gSASRec (2023; IJCAI 2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes instability to overconfidence from sampled BCE and combines more negatives with generalized BCE. This supports comparing multi-negative sampled softmax against both ordinary BCE and gBCE, rather than assuming contrastive training necessarily wins. The [RecSys 2025 LogQ authors’ implementation](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides directly comparable SASRec variants: full softmax, uniform sampled softmax, in-batch negatives, mixed uniform/in-batch sampling, and original versus revised sampling corrections. Nonuniform sampling therefore warrants an explicit correction ablation.

Hardest-negative selection can backfire. [R2NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports early training failures with aggressive hard mining; uniform warm-up followed by stochastic selection among high-scoring candidates improves stability. High-scoring unobserved items can also be false negatives. Practical experiment proposal: compare 32–128 uniform negatives with a modest hard-negative mixture after warm-up, mask known training positives and accidental target collisions, and tune hardness conservatively. These are hypotheses for this benchmark; the cited evidence does not establish Electronics-specific gains.

Select exclusively by the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10, inspecting Electronics separately for tradeoffs. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation. Consequently, published full-ranking improvements, lower training loss, or larger margins cannot establish improvement under the pinned 99-negative evaluator; keep its users, candidates, seed, and metric unchanged.
